input.summary: Add frequency, notice, cost and system-access limits to IBM's investigation right in § 11.3
input.comment: [Playbook] IBM's right to investigate suspected AUP violations is currently unlimited and unannounced, so we have added our standard guardrails: once per 12 months, 30 days' written notice, business hours, IBM's cost, an auditor bound by confidentiality and no access to our systems, with a carve-out for ongoing violations posing imminent harm. If helpful we can fall back to 15 days' notice.

ops.text: Any investigation by IBM under this Subsection 11.3 will be conducted no more than once in any twelve (12) month period, on at least thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Customer, during Customer's normal business hours, at IBM's expense, and by IBM or an independent auditor bound by written obligations of confidentiality. No such investigation will include access to Customer's systems, networks or premises, and IBM will have no remote access to Customer systems for investigation purposes. The foregoing notice and frequency limitations do not apply where IBM reasonably believes that a violation is ongoing and poses an imminent risk of harm to the e-business Hosting Environment or to a third party.
